confidence_notes: I ran four web searches: one for the RBA rate and three for Orlando food and drink prices. Restaurant meals, cappuccino and beer rest on aggregated Numbeo-based figures: about $22 for an inexpensive meal, about $89 for a mid-range meal for two, about $5.2 for a cappuccino and about $6 for a domestic draft. I rounded the beer anchor up slightly for tourist-area restaurant pricing. Cocktail and wine did not have a reliable citywide average. The cocktail anchor draws on one crowd-sourced Expatistan figure of about $15 for a downtown club, plus my general knowledge that full-price tourist-area cocktails run $12-18. The wine-glass anchor is a general-knowledge estimate of $12-16, informed by the cocktail and beer relationship (roughly 2x beer) and happy-hour listings that were discounted. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from live listings or booking pages. Orlando has few registered hostels, and hotel rates vary a lot with theme-park demand, resort fees and location (International Drive, Kissimmee, downtown), so the hostel and hotel anchors are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Orlando is a large US tourist-driven market with slightly above-average US living costs (index around 104). Its restaurant prices run below Washington DC and above smaller Florida cities. The cocktail and wine anchors use typical US mid-tier tourist-city relationships to beer.
